name: Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport
before:
Shanghai's closer airport, 13 km west of downtown, and the one to choose when a client wants to be in the city quickly. It handled 50,151,025 passengers in 2025, eighth busiest in China, and holds a Skytrax five star rating.

The real advantage is the railway. Terminal 2 sits directly beside Shanghai Hongqiao railway station, which is served by the Beijing to Shanghai, Shanghai to Hangzhou and Shanghai to Nanjing high speed lines, so a flight here connects straight onto high speed rail without a road transfer. Three metro stations serve the airport and the station between them.

Note that Terminal 1 is on the far side of the airfield from Terminal 2, with its own metro station on Line 10, so check which terminal a flight uses.

Since December 2024 the Airport Link Line has provided a direct rail connection to Pudong, which makes a two airport itinerary far easier than it used to be.

Hongqiao was Shanghai's main airport until Pudong opened in October 1999. It is the headquarters of China Eastern Airlines and a hub for Shanghai Airlines, Juneyao Air and Spring Airlines.
after:
Shanghai's closer airport is 13 km west of downtown and the one to choose when a client wants to be in the city quickly. Its 50,151,025 passengers in 2025 made it the eighth busiest in China, and it holds a Skytrax five star rating.

The real advantage is the railway. Hongqiao Airport sits at the centre of a transport hub with a high speed railway station, Shanghai Hongqiao, so a flight here connects onto high speed rail. Metro Lines 2 and 10 serve Terminal 2.

Note that Terminal 1 has its own metro station on Line 10, which links it with Terminal 2, so check which terminal a flight uses.

Since December 2024 the Airport Link Line has provided a direct rail connection to Pudong, which makes a two airport itinerary far easier than it used to be.

China Eastern Airlines, Shanghai Airlines and Spring Airlines all fly from here.

claims.claim: the airport is at the centre of a transport hub with a high speed railway station, Shanghai Hongqiao
claims.inAfter: Hongqiao Airport sits at the centre of a transport hub with a high speed railway station, Shanghai Hongqiao, so a flight here connects onto high speed rail
claims.note: Was 'Terminal 2 sits directly beside Shanghai Hongqiao railway station ... so a flight here connects straight onto high speed rail without a road transfer'. Sixth Tone (a Shanghai news outlet, March 2021, for the airport's centenary) calls the airport the centre of a transport hub built with a high-speed rail station; the Shanghai government's May 2026 visitor routes start from 'Hongqiao International Airport/Hongqiao Railway Station' as one place, and its train guide names Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station. That Terminal 2 in particular is 'directly beside' the station, 'without a road transfer', rests on Wikipedia alone, so it is softened to the hub.

claims.note: Was 'Three metro stations serve the airport and the station between them'. The operator and the Shanghai government name the two terminal stations only; the third, Hongqiao Railway Station on Lines 2, 10 and 17, rests on Wikipedia alone. The operator's Hongqiao metro entries were last updated in April 2024; the government's copy was updated on 4 June 2026. On the operator's site: OurAirports and Wikipedia link shairport.com, which answered with a script challenge (HTTP 521); shanghaiairport.com is the Authority's current site, since its disclosure page (op-cn-jbxx) gives the company's English name as 'Shanghai Airport Authority', its pages give @shairport.com contact addresses, and the Shanghai government's airport guide cites it as the Authority's page. After about ten requests it began serving the same 521 challenge, and it was not tried again.

The operator's own site (shanghaiairport.com) began answering with a script challenge (HTTP 521) before its arrivals and hub pages could be read, the older shairport.com gave the same challenge from the first request, the Hongqiao business district's English site answered 502 and its 2025 report (a PDF) timed out.

claims.claim: Hongqiao was Shanghai's main airport until Pudong opened in October 1999
claims.wasBefore: Hongqiao was Shanghai's main airport until Pudong opened in October 1999.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. Four tries found no second source: the operator's heritage page came back empty and then 502 in the browser, the transport commission's September 2026 Pudong article, The Paper's 2020 history piece and Sixth Tone's centenary report give no Pudong opening date, and the Shanghai government portals have no airport history page that could be found without a search.

claims.wasBefore: It is the headquarters of China Eastern Airlines
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. China Eastern's own site (ceair.com) builds its pages by script and showed no links to the browser; the operator's airlines page answered with the same script challenge (521). China Eastern flying from Hongqiao is kept (see above).

claims.claim: a hub for Shanghai Airlines, Juneyao Air and Spring Airlines
claims.wasBefore: a hub for Shanghai Airlines, Juneyao Air and Spring Airlines
claims.why: 'Hub' rests on Wikipedia alone (Spring Airlines' own page lists bases in other cities and its head office in Shanghai, not a Hongqiao hub). Juneyao Air rests on Wikipedia alone: its site gave a bare script shell to a plain fetch (368 bytes) and the browser try was refused by the session's proxy, which does not carry plain-http requests, so it had its two tries. Shanghai Airlines and Spring Airlines are kept as flying from here (see above).

claims.claim: Hongqiao mainly handles domestic flights plus regional flights within East Asia
claims.note: Found while checking the airport's role: the Shanghai government's airport guide (from the Airport Authority, June 2026) says Hongqiao 'primarily serves domestic flights and regional flights within East Asia', while Pudong handles both international and domestic flights; Wikipedia names five international routes (Haneda, Gimpo, Songshan, Hong Kong, Macau); Skytrax calls it 'the best, large domestic airport in China'. This matters to a UK agent: no flight from the UK lands here, so a UK client reaches Hongqiao on a domestic or regional connection.
